science.title: Scientists restore a brain protein and reverse signs of aging in mice
science.description: Scientists found that declining levels of the brain protein Menin may help drive aging, with lower levels in mice linked to inflammation, cognitive decline, weaker bones, and thinner skin. Restoring Menin reversed several age-related changes, while the amino acid D-serine improved cognition, hinting at a potentially intriguing new target for healthy aging.

science.title: Tree bark home to methane
science.description: A UN report in September said global heating will hit 1.8C — at least — but this could be partially reversed by removing carbon from the atmosphere. One way to achieve this is by establishing vast new forests. Trees take carbon dioxide from the air for photosynthesis, and it turns out microbes living in tree bark can absorb another potent greenhouse gas, methane. Shelby Traynor meets two researchers investigating the microbial world within tree bark.
science.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

science.title: What Did Jurassic Forests Sound Like? Scientists Recreated Prehistoric Soundscape & Discovered Ultrasonic Wave
science.description: Scientists have successfully reconstructed the 165-million-year-old prehistoric calls of Jurassic insects, unlocking rare acoustic insights into the soundscape of the Middle Jurassic era. This groundbreaking paleoacoustic research recreates the long-lost vocalizations of ancient Jurassic insects, offering a unique window into the auditory world of prehistoric life that roamed Earth 165 million years ago. The landmark study of fossil-based sound reconstruction brings the once-silent Jurassic period’s natural acoustic environment to life, marking a major breakthrough in exploring prehistoric insect behavior and the evolutionary history of animal communication sounds dating back to 165 million years.
